paper.title: Transvaginal ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics for preoperative identification of non-endometrioid endometrial carcinoma: A multicenter study.
paper.abstract:
Objective: Preoperative identification of non-endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (NEEC) is clinically important because non-endometrioid histology may influence risk assessment and treatment planning. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a transvaginal ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics (DLR) model for preoperative identification of NEEC.
Methods: A total of 663 patients with pathologically confirmed endometrial carcinoma from 11 centers were retrospectively included. The training cohort consisted of 483 patients from eight centers, including 161 NEEC and 322 EEC cases. An independent external test cohort included 180 patients from three additional centers, including 60 NEEC and 120 EEC cases. Radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics, and deep learning features were extracted using ResNet-101. Radiomics, deep learning, and combined DLR models were developed using machine learning classifiers and evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and external validation.
Results: The combined DLR model achieved the best diagnostic performance among the three models. In the external test cohort, the DLR model yielded an AUC of 0.837, with an accuracy of 0.756, sensitivity of 0.800, and specificity of 0.733. The DLR model outperformed the radiomics model and the deep learning model in both the training and external test cohorts.
Conclusion: The transvaginal ultrasound-based DLR model showed potential as a noninvasive tool for preoperative identification of NEEC. This model may provide complementary information for individualized preoperative assessment, although prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

paper.title: An explainable artificial intelligence system for prognostic assessment and decision support in diabetic foot ulcer care: a multicentre derivation and validation study with prospective randomised evaluation.
paper.abstract:
Background: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) carry risks of recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality, but most prediction models address single outcomes and have limited interpretability. We developed an interpretable multi-outcome machine-learning framework for individualised DFU risk assessment and prospective clinical evaluation.
Methods: We conducted a development and validation study across three hospitals in China from January 1, 2018, to April 30, 2025. We used electronic medical records and follow-up data from 763 patients at Centres A and B to develop and internally validate an ensemble of single-task extreme gradient boosting (ST-XGBoost) and single-task multilayer perceptron (ST-MLP) models to predict cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality. The locked ensemble was externally validated in 100 patients at Centre C. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, with interpretability evaluated using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). From January 5 to March 5, 2026, we performed a prospective comparative evaluation. We randomised 202 participants (1:1) to usual care or artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted care, of whom 200 were analysed. We compared AI-assisted physician decision-making via an evolvable web-based online prediction platform versus usual care. The outcome was overall quality score of the final clinical recommendation. The platform supports follow-up data collection for future offline model updating.
Findings: In the training dataset, cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality occurred in 638, 208, 226, and 167 patients, respectively; the corresponding numbers in the external validation dataset were 80, 34, 24, and 25. In independent external validation, the ST-XGBoost + ST-MLP ensemble outperformed six comparators, with a macro-averaged AUC of 0.901, accuracy of 0.875, and F1 score of 0.830. Outcome-specific discrimination was highest for amputation (AUC 0.953) and all-cause mortality (AUC 0.951), followed by cure (AUC 0.880) and recurrence (AUC 0.820). In the prospective evaluation, AI-assisted recommendations received higher scores than corresponding clinician recommendations (7.77 vs 6.47; mean difference 1.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.08-1.52; p < 0.0001), with the largest gain in completeness. The AI-assisted group showed better short-term follow-up engagement and glucose-management adherence.
Interpretation: We demonstrate that integrating gradient-boosted trees and neural networks enables explainable prediction of complex DFU trajectories and may support prioritised, individualised clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, recurrence estimates should be interpreted cautiously.
Funding: Xuzhou Municipal Health Commission Science and Technology Project (XWYHT20240128).

paper.title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning‑based Prediction Model for ICU‑Acquired Weakness in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
paper.abstract:
Background: ICU-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) is a common and devastating complication of critical illness associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation and increased mortality, whereas externally validated tools for early risk stratification remain insufficient. This study aimed to construct and validate machine learning models to predict ICU-AW risk in critically ill patients.
Methods: A total of 535 patients from three medical centers were divided into a training set (n = 276), an internal validation set (n = 119) and an external validation cohort (n = 140). Candidate predictors were restricted to variables available within the first 48 hours of ICU admission. Five algorithms including logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), classification and regression tree (CART) and XGBoost were trained with 10-fold cross-validated grid search and compared using DeLong tests. Six predictors were retained: age, Glasgow Coma Scale score, SOFA score, sepsis, renal failure and hypoalbuminemia.
Results: All five models displayed favorable predictive capacity in the internal validation set (AUROC 0.906-0.939). In external validation, SVM (0.853, 95% CI 0.779-0.915) and LR (0.841, 0.765-0.906) outperformed RF (0.802), XGBoost (0.790) and CART (0.685), and the difference between SVM and LR was not statistically significant (DeLong P = 0.085). Tree-based algorithms presented near-perfect apparent performance that attenuated markedly in the external cohort, indicating overfitting. The LR model, which offered statistically comparable discrimination with full transparency, was converted into a nomogram (external AUROC 0.841) with positive net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities of 1-81%.
Conclusion: A six-predictor logistic model based on variables available within 48 hours of ICU admission predicted ICU-AW comparably to tuned machine learning classifiers and showed stable cross-center performance. The nomogram may assist early risk stratification, and prospective studies are warranted to confirm whether model-guided care improves patient outcomes.

paper.title: EGFR mutation prediction in NSCLC from CT images via self-supervised disentangled feature learning and multimodal fusion.
paper.abstract:
Background: Computed tomography (CT)-based noninvasive prediction of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is highly important for advancing precision diagnosis and treatment. Current detection methods that rely on invasive tissue biopsies present several limitations. This study aimed to develop a model that integrated deep learning and multimodal information for the noninvasive prediction of EGFR-sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletion and L858R point mutation) in NSCLC patients using contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) images.
Methods: We retrospectively included 466 pathologically confirmed NSCLC patients from two centers (413 from our own center for model development and internal validation, and 53 from another center for independent external validation), and proposed a novel paradigm combining disentangled self-supervised learning (D-SSL) with multimodal gated fusion. The D-SSL encoder was pretrained on CT images and tumor ROI masks from the entire 413-patient internal cohort without using EGFR mutation labels and was subsequently fixed for downstream classification. An adaptive gated fusion network was subsequently constructed to dynamically integrate these deep features with traditional radiomics features and clinical information to predict the EGFR-sensitizing mutation status.
Results: In 20 repeated random splits, the D-SSL fusion models achieved mean AUCs of 0.800 (±0.052) and 0.794 (±0.048) on the training set and internal test set, respectively. One-way ANOVA and subsequent Tukey HSD post-hoc test revealed that the performance on the internal test set of the D-SSL fusion models was significantly superior to that of the clinical models, radiomics models, and radiomics-clinical fusion models (all p < 0.001). On the fully independent external validation set, which was not involved in D-SSL pretraining or downstream model development, the D-SSL fusion models maintained robust performance with a mean AUC of 0.680 (±0.038). Ablation studies showed that models using only the shape head or only the texture head achieved mean AUCs of 0.680 (±0.023) and 0.684 (±0.028), respectively, both significantly lower than that of the complete D-SSL fusion models (both p < 0.001), confirming the complementarity of shape and texture features. Subgroup analysis demonstrated that the model achieved accuracies significantly above the random chance level (50%) in female 83.65% (±3.97%), male 68.90% (±3.72%), smoker 85.07% (±4.41%), and nonsmoker 69.21% (±3.44%) subgroups, suggesting that it did not merely rely on clinical features but captured deep imaging phenotypes associated with EGFR-sensitizing mutations. Feature visualization analysis demonstrated that the D-SSL feature space could effectively distinguish among various imaging manifestation types and pathological categories, confirming the model's ability to capture highly discriminative and clinically meaningful imaging phenotypes.
Conclusions: This study developed a framework integrating D-SSL and multimodal fusion for the noninvasive prediction of EGFR-sensitizing mutations in NSCLC. The framework demonstrated strong discrimination in the internal transductive evaluation and retained predictive value in a fully independent external cohort. These findings support the potential of self-supervised representation learning and gated multimodal fusion, while larger multicenter studies using strictly inductive split-before-pretraining designs remain necessary.

paper.title: Development and evaluation of a breast cancer risk stratification tool for women in Macau.
paper.abstract:
Background: Widely used breast cancer risk prediction tools are predominantly based on data from Western countries, and their predictive efficacy in Asian women is often questioned, partly due to ethnic differences in risk factors. This study aimed to develop and temporally validate the Macau Breast Cancer Risk Stratification Tool (MBC-RST), based on non-laboratory-detectable indicators.
Methods: This multi-stage study involved the development and temporal validation of the MBC-RST. Phase 1 involved a literature review and retrospective analysis of 14,111 local health questionnaires to create an initial 17-item tool (MBC-RST_Version 1) with expert consultation. In Phase 2, this version was pilot-tested on 10,691 women, while a more detailed cross-sectional survey (MBC-RS) was administered to 1,321 women. Machine learning (specifically LightGBM) and statistical analyses were used to identify additional predictive factors, leading to an optimized 21-item tool (MBC-RST_Version 2). Phase 3 involved the launch and performance evaluation of MBC-RST_Version 2 using data from 9,985 new participants.
Results: The initial retrospective analysis identified significant risk factors including age (OR = 1.09), delayed age at menarche (OR = 0.90), presence of a breast lump (OR = 22.2), and unilateral nipple discharge (OR = 2.14). The subsequent factor analysis and machine learning analysis on prospective data identified 'pregnancy history,' 'age at first childbirth,' 'number of miscarriages,' and 'exercise intensity' as highly important predictors. These factors were integrated into the final 21-item tool. The final MBC-RST_Version 2, evaluated on a total of 25,476 participants, demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.7% (95% CI: 72.4%-94.3%) and a specificity of 89.4% (95% CI: 89.0%-89.8%). The tool significantly enhances screening efficiency; it is estimated that only 136 imaging examinations are needed to detect one positive case in the high-risk group, compared to 326 in an age-based universal screening approach.
Conclusion: This study developed and temporally validated the MBC-RST, a 21-item tool tailored for Macau women which is practical, accessible, and scientifically robust. The MBC-RST showed promising performance in a temporally separated cohort recruited within the same Macau healthcare system. For broader clinical or population-level implementation of this tool, validation in a geographically or institutionally independent population is required.
